news.title: Bayern Munich’s Manuel Neuer on ‘very bitter’ World Cup exit
news.lede: Retirement has been a topic hovering around Manuel Neuer lately. The legendary goalkeeper came out of international retirement for a last run with Germany this summer, which ended in heartbreak at the Men’s World Cup. And the upcoming Bayern Munich season may be his last. But the 40-year-old just can’t get enough of football so far — and that’s a good thing.

news.title: Entain scores a World Cup win
news.lede: Eastern European arm is up for sale. Interim results for Entain (ENT) came in better than analysts expected. Underlying cash profit was £10mn lower at £479mn – a credible performance given the hit to earnings following an increase in the UK’s online gambling tax rates. Broker Shore Capital had expected an underlying Ebitda decline of £40mn.

news.title: Why half of England's World Cup defenders are on the move
news.lede: Will Djed Spence (left) and Ezri Konsa (middle) be the next England players to be involved in transfers this summer? England came third in this summer's World Cup - their best performance in a men's competition in 60 years - and now their players are in demand in the transfer market. Of the 27 players that went out to North America - 26 in the original squad and Trevoh Chalobah, who replaced the injured Tino Livramento - seven have moved clubs this summer, with another two linked with transfers. Morgan Rogers went from Aston Villa to Chelsea in a £117m deal, midfielder Elliot Anderson moved for £116m from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City and winger Anthony Gordon cost Barcelona almost £70m when transferring from Newcastle.

news.title: Republic of Ireland: Pairc Ui Chaoimh to host Women's World Cup play-off with Kazakhstan
news.lede: The Republic of Ireland have a 100% winning record at Pairc Ui Chaoimh in Cork. The home leg of the Republic of Ireland's 2027 Women's World Cup play-off with Kazakhstan will be played at Pairc Ui Chaoimh in Cork. Carla Ward's side travel to Kazakhstan on 9 October before the return fixture at the home of Gaelic games in Cork on Tuesday, 13 October. The winner of the first round play-off will face either Belgium or Poland for a place in the World Cup in Brazil next summer.

news.title: South Korea's Football Assoc. Bribed International Referees With Escorts During World Cup Qualifiers In The Early 2010s: Report
news.lede: The KFA has apologized for bribing refs with escort services. The Korea Football Association has issued a public apology after it was reported that it had bribed referees with escort services in the early 2010s. South Korea has qualified for 11 straight World Cups since 1986. According to a government report that was recently made public, the Korea Football Association (KFA) spent approximately $3,950 (5.6 million Korean won) on sexual services for foreign referees on eight separate occasions surrounding World Cup and Olympic qualifying matches between 2011 and 2012.

news.title: ‘This was my World Cup’ says Somali referee Omar Artan after Super Cup final
news.lede: Somali referee Omar Artan calls the UEFA Super Cup his "World Cup" after being denied entry to the actual tournament.
